newsitem.title: USA: Insurer USF&G reports drop in profits.
newsitem.headline: Insurer USF&G reports drop in profits.

text.p: USF&G Corp., one of the nation's biggest property and casualty insurers, Wednesday reported a 13 percent drop in second-quarter operating income, as it made an $18 million provision for income taxes.
The Baltimore-based holding company posted operating income of 48 million, or 40 cents a share, compared with $54 million, or 41 cents a share, in 1996's second quarter.
The results beat the consensus Wall Street forecast of 38 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks analyst estimates.
USF&G had earnings of $47 million, or 42 cents per share, on revenues of $872 million vs. net income of $67 million, or 67 cents a share, on revenues of $858 million last year.
USF&G's profitable growth returned it to tax-reporting status this year, resulting in the $18 million income tax provision, Chairman Norman Blake Jr. said in a statement.
Blake said the 1996 second-quarter results included a one-time $12 million gain from a property tax adjustment.
Revenues in the latest period included $691 million in premiums, compared with $674 million in the 1996 period.
For the first half of 1997, USF&G had operating income of $95 million, or 76 cents a share, vs. $98 million, or 74 cents a share in 1996. Revenues rose to $1.4 billion from $1.3 billion.
"USF&G's second-quarter results demonstrate the continuing success of our strategies to improve the underwriting performance and profitability of our four business units," Blake said.

The company's principal subsidiary is United States Fidelity and Guaranty, founded in 1896 and one of the nation's biggest property and casualty insurers. Its units also include Fidelity and Guaranty Life Insurance.
The company's stock was unchanged at $24.81 in composite early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
